title: Identifying Training Needs & Evaluating Training
overview: The effectiveness of a training function is largely dependent on accurately identifying training needs and evaluating the impact of training programs. This course is designed to shift decision-making around training from subjective to objective, relying on proven methodologies. Such a shift enhances the value of the training department within an organization. Additionally, the course focuses on building an understanding of evaluation techniques, ranging from commonly used evaluation forms to more advanced methods assessing skills transfer and return on investment (ROI).
audience: This course is ideal for administrators, officers, specialists, team leaders, managers, business partners, and line managers who are responsible for identifying training needs or evaluating training in their organizations.
methodology: The course is highly practical and interactive, combining theoretical concepts with hands-on exercises that allow participants to apply their learning in real-world organizational contexts.
objectivesIntro: By the end of the course, participants will be able to:
objectives: Use internationally recognized methods for identifying training needs
Analyze and organize data from a Training Needs Assessment (TNA)
Write clear and aligned Instructional Learning Objectives (ILOs) based on TNA results
Evaluate training effectiveness at different levels, utilizing appropriate data collection techniques and tools
Identify ways to improve the transfer of skills from training sessions to the workplace
Calculate ROI for training programs by assessing their financial impact and returns
